summary: The XRD analysis in this paper confirms the formation of cubic-phase CsPbBr3 nanocrystals (NCs) with characteristic peaks at 15.2°, 21.6°, and 30.6°. The peaks are broad, consistent with nanoscale crystallite size. Only one XRD figure is provided, limiting the ability to assess trends with processing or sample variation.

key_findings.finding: XRD patterns of colloidal CsPbBr3 nanocrystals show peaks at 15.2°, 21.6°, and 30.6°, corresponding to the (100), (110), and (200) planes of the cubic phase.
The XRD peaks are broad, indicating nanocrystalline size.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The colloidal CsPbBr3 nanocrystals synthesized in this study possess a cubic perovskite structure.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The caption and text explicitly state that the observed XRD peaks correspond to the cubic phase of CsPbBr3.

citations.evidence: From the XRD patterns (Fig. 2d ), the (100), (110), and (200) peaks demonstrated the cubic crystal structure of CsPbBr 3 NCs.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The broadness of the XRD peaks suggests the CsPbBr3 nanocrystals are of small (nanoscale) size.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The analysis notes broad peaks, which is characteristic of nanocrystalline materials due to size broadening effects.

limitations.claim: Only a single XRD pattern is provided, so no comparison across different synthesis conditions or sample treatments is possible.

limitations.claim: No quantitative crystallite size estimation is possible due to missing FWHM data.
No evidence is provided for phase purity beyond the assignment of the main peaks; possible minor phases or impurities cannot be ruled out.
